record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: Consider the nonlinear Loewner-type evolution ∂_t f(z,t) = z f′(z,t) ∫_T ((z+ζ)/(z-ζ)) |dζ| / |f′(ζ,t)|^α. For small |α| and for natural classes of initial conformal maps φ, does this evolution admit a satisfactory existence and uniqueness theory?

evidence.quote: Does the problem (4.1) enjoy a good existence and uniqueness theory for |α| small and for some natural classes of initial conditions φ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk and $\mathbb{T}=\partial\mathbb{D}$ its boundary, equipped with arc-length measure $|d\zeta|$. For a real parameter $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|$ small, consider the nonlinear Loewner-type evolution equation for a family of conformal maps $f(\cdot,t):\mathbb{D}\to\Omega_t\subset\mathbb{C}$, $t\ge 0$:
$$\partial_t f(z,t) \;=\; z\,f'(z,t)\int_{\mathbb{T}} \frac{z+\zeta}{z-\zeta}\,\frac{|d\zeta|}{|f'(\zeta,t)|^{\alpha}},\qquad z\in\mathbb{D},$$
with initial condition $f(z,0)=\varphi(z)$, where $\varphi:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ is a univalent (conformal) map and $f'$ denotes the derivative in the spatial variable $z$. The boundary integrand $1/|f'(\zeta,t)|^{\alpha}$ is to be interpreted in a suitable boundary trace sense.

Question: Does this evolution admit a satisfactory existence and uniqueness theory for $|\alpha|$ sufficiently small, within natural classes of initial conformal maps $\varphi$ (for instance, those whose image has smooth boundary, or bounded boundary derivative away from $0$ and $\infty$)? In particular, identify a class of initial data and a notion of solution for which local-in-time existence and uniqueness hold, and determine whether the solutions extend globally in time.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on regularized Hastings–Levitov aggregation and Loewner–Kufarev type equations has established existence/uniqueness and scaling-limit results in subcritical parameter regimes (e.g., $\zeta=\alpha+\eta\le 1$), which covers the small-$|\alpha|$ regime for regularized variants. However, a complete existence/uniqueness theory for the unregularized continuum evolution with the boundary integrand $|f'(\zeta,t)|^{-\alpha}$ on $\mathbb{T}$ remains incomplete; full treatment of natural classes of initial conformal maps is not yet settled.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Regularized Hastings–Levitov Aggregation in the Subcritical Regime
status_evidence.snippet: Two-parameter class of continuum planar aggregation models; limit dynamics follow a Loewner–Kufarev equation; subcriticality condition ζ ≤ 1.
status_evidence.claim: Existence/scaling-limit results are available in the subcritical regime relevant to small α, supporting partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Loewner–Kufarev entropy and large deviations of the Hastings–Levitov model
status_evidence.snippet: Analysis of Loewner–Kufarev equations driving Hastings–Levitov type aggregation.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on the well-posedness and large-deviation theory of this Loewner-type evolution.

status_evidence.title: Aggregation in the Plane and Loewner's Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces aggregation Loewner-type evolutions of the stated form and poses well-posedness questions.
status_evidence.claim: The well-posedness problem for this evolution was explicitly raised and remains a guiding open question.
